facts.detail: Ofcom last updated the broadband-switching guide on 1 July 2026.
Broadband switching uses the One Touch Switch process.
The customer contacts the provider they want to move to and the new provider arranges the switch.
The customer supplies details including the services to switch, address and current provider name.
The One Touch Switch process tells customers about applicable early termination charges.

guard_streams.source: What to do if your broadband or landline provider goes out of business

facts.detail: Ofcom published the provider-failure guidance on 13 February 2026.
When another company takes over, service should usually continue without interruption.
The existing contract should usually transfer to the new provider.
If the new provider changes contract terms, customers should have the right to leave without an early termination charge.
If there is no takeover, service will stop on a notified date and the customer must sign up with a new provider without an early termination charge.

facts.detail: Ofcom last updated the broadband and landline faults guide on 8 April 2026.
The guide covers slower broadband, connection problems and phone-line faults.
Recent changes to wiring or equipment around the home can affect broadband speed.
Telephone extension leads can cause interference and reduce speed.
Microfilters should be fitted to every telephone socket in use so phone and broadband signals do not interfere.

facts.detail: Ofcom last updated the provider-selection guidance on 10 February 2026.
Ofcom combines information from residential customers and providers to describe service quality.
The page provides an interactive comparison of major mobile, broadband and home-phone providers.
Mobile signal varies with distance from masts and with buildings or natural obstacles.
Broadband contract cost can depend on delivery technology, headline speed, extras, contract length and installation fees.

facts.detail: Ofcom last updated the Communications Affordability Tracker on 14 May 2026.
The tracker covers affordability experiences for home broadband, mobile, landline and pay-TV services.

The page notes that 36% of October 2025 participants did not know or declined to report household income.
